summary_hint: bureaus, pull date, the three scores, and tradeline/public-record/inquiry counts

typed_core.name: borrower_name
typed_core.why: identity — whose report; attaches the document to a borrower; the subject for ID-2/ID-4/RE-1

typed_core.name: co_borrower_name
typed_core.why: a joint or merged report carries a second subject; attribution for ID-2/ID-4

typed_core.name: borrower_ssn
typed_core.why: ID-2 — 'EXACT match, no fuzzy'. Stored raw so the snapshot can salt-hash for cross-document matching
typed_core.prompt_hint: Never place an SSN in additional_sections — catch-all values are stored unmasked

typed_core.name: co_borrower_ssn
typed_core.why: ID-2 for the second subject on a joint pull

typed_core.name: borrower_date_of_birth
typed_core.why: identity disambiguator — distinguishes two same-name subjects; a secondary ID cross-check

typed_core.name: borrower_current_address
typed_core.why: ID-4 — current-address consistency against the application, bank statement and pay stub

typed_core.name: borrower_former_address
typed_core.why: disambiguator for ID-4 — reports list prior addresses, so an apparent mismatch may be a known former address
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish CURRENT from FORMER — never report a former address as current

typed_core.name: report_date
typed_core.why: CR-13 — 'closing_date minus report_date vs the validity window'. The single field CR-13 exists to read
typed_core.prompt_hint: The PULL/issue date, not the score as-of date

typed_core.name: score_date
typed_core.why: disambiguator — the score as-of date can differ from the pull date; CR-13 must use the pull date

typed_core.name: report_provider
typed_core.why: identity — the reseller/CRA that issued the merge (CoreLogic, Factual Data); distinguishes two pulls

typed_core.name: report_reference_number
typed_core.why: identity — distinguishes reissues for the same borrower

typed_core.name: credit_report_type
typed_core.why: CR-7 disambiguator — tri-merge vs single-bureau decides middle-of-three vs lower-of-two

typed_core.name: score_equifax
typed_core.why: CR-7, PE-1 — one of the three inputs to the representative score

typed_core.name: score_experian
typed_core.why: CR-7, PE-1

typed_core.name: score_transunion
typed_core.why: CR-7, PE-1

typed_core.name: score_model
typed_core.why: CR-7 disambiguator — FICO v2/v4/v5 (mortgage classic) vs FICO 8 vs VantageScore are NOT comparable to a program minimum
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the model exactly as printed. Beacon = Equifax FICO; Empirica = TransUnion FICO. Never compare a Vantage score to a FICO minimum

typed_core.name: tradeline_count
typed_core.why: DT-7 completeness signal, and a cross-check against the length of the tradelines list

typed_core.name: total_monthly_debt_payment
typed_core.why: DT-7, supports CR-4 — the report's summed monthly obligations, reconciled against the application's stated liabilities

typed_core.name: public_record_count
typed_core.why: presence gate for CR-6/CR-11 — a cheap 'are there any?' before walking the list

typed_core.name: inquiry_count
typed_core.why: presence gate for CR-5 — how many hard inquiries need an LOE or matching tradeline

typed_core.name: security_freeze_or_fraud_alert
typed_core.why: processor — a freeze or fraud alert blocks a clean pull and is a common condition

nested_lists.name: tradelines
nested_lists.shape_reason: a tri-merge routinely carries 20+ tradelines; per-field wrapping would risk the 16,384-token output ceiling

fields.name: account_number_masked
fields.pii_note: pre-masked last-4; the nested list needs a row redactor, not _PII_FIELDS

fields.name: account_ownership
fields.why: CR-4 — ECOA individual/joint/authorized-user. An AU tradeline is NOT the borrower's obligation

fields.name: date_opened
fields.why: CR-5 — matching an inquiry to a resulting new account

fields.name: credit_limit_or_high_credit
fields.why: CR-2 — HCLTV uses the limit, not the balance

fields.name: payment_history_24mo
fields.why: CR-8 — 'recent lates against program tolerance'. A COMPACT STRING, never 24 sub-objects

fields.name: is_disputed
fields.why: CR-12 — 'detect dispute flags; flag for AUS rerun'

nested_lists.name: public_records
nested_lists.shape_reason: typically 0-5 items; flat rows keep the token cost trivial

fields.name: record_type
fields.why: CR-6 — bankruptcy chapter / tax lien / judgment

fields.name: filing_date
fields.why: CR-6 — the seasoning clock's start for a lien or judgment

fields.name: discharge_or_satisfied_date
fields.why: CR-6 — for a bankruptcy, seasoning runs from DISCHARGE, not filing

nested_lists.name: inquiries
nested_lists.shape_reason: typically 0-10 items; flat rows keep the token cost trivial

fields.name: creditor_name
fields.why: CR-5 — matching an inquiry to a resulting tradeline

fields.name: inquiry_type
fields.why: CR-5 — ONLY hard inquiries count; soft pulls are excluded

rejected.name: representative_score
rejected.reason: a conclusion — CR-7 COMPUTES it (middle-of-three / lower-of-two) from the three bureau scores. Tags describe; rules judge

rejected.name: has_derogatory / derogatory_count
rejected.reason: a conclusion — CR-6 judges seasoning from public_records

rejected.name: large_collection_flag
rejected.reason: a conclusion — CR-10 applies program thresholds

rejected.name: dti / total_debt_ratio
rejected.reason: not on a credit report; computed downstream from income and liabilities

rejected.name: total_open_balance
rejected.reason: a summary with no rule consumer; balances live per tradeline

rejected.name: employment_history (bureau-reported)
rejected.reason: unreliable and stale; IN-4/IN-5 use the 1003 and pay stubs

encoding_variations: Every bureau formats differently; a tri-merge from Factual Data reads nothing like one from CBC
Scores are labelled differently per bureau — Equifax 'Beacon', TransUnion 'FICO Classic/Risk', Experian 'FICO v2'. The MODEL must ride alongside the number
Report date, score as-of date, and 'in file since' date can all appear; CR-13 needs the PULL date
Collections may appear as a tradeline with a status code, in a separate collections section, or as a public record — the same fact in three locations
Bankruptcy: chapter 7 vs 13, and filed / discharged / dismissed dates differ. Seasoning runs from the DISCHARGE date
Disputes appear as 'consumer disputes this account', compliance codes (XB/XC), or free-text remarks — no single flag
MOP (Manner of Payment) codes 1-9 encode delinquency
ECOA codes govern ownership: Individual / Joint / Authorized User / Co-signer

open_questions.q: Three nested lists (~15 plumbing sites) — ship all now or phase?
options: tradelines only, defer public_records and inquiries
open_questions.recommendation: all three — CR-5/CR-6/CR-11 are otherwise dead, and both extra lists are small (0-5 items), so the token cost is minor GEET'S DECISION (LP-435): build ALL THREE nested lists (tradelines, public_records, inquiries).

open_questions.q: SSN storage vs ID-2's exact match
open_questions.recommendation: raw + snapshot hash — a last-4 mask defeats the 'differs in the first five digits' case ID-2 exists to catch

open_questions.q: Token ceiling on a large report
open_questions.recommendation: test against a real 30-page tri-merge before committing; 20+ tradelines x 14 fields plus two more lists is the largest output in the set
capture as tradelines AND let CR-10 scan public_records; document the dual location for the rule author

open_questions.q: How does the report enter the system?
open_questions.recommendation: processor upload — confirmed; classification and routing are the standard path

notes: NO v2 catalog entry exists for this document — the rule floor IS the entire schema. Every field is therefore rule_floor: true.
The largest single unlock in the project: 11 of its 14 rules are BLOCKED on this extractor.
The most PII-dense document in a mortgage file. _PII_FIELDS covers typed-core only; anything in additional_sections is stored UNMASKED.
No PiiKind exists today for DOB or ADDRESS — both are needed here (see also the 1003).
A nested-list PII field has no _PII_FIELDS path; the transaction-description redactor is the precedent for per-row redaction.
